solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Problem horse may have with birds bearing left

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the birds hold the letter for left within them

parts.note: ganders are male geese

explanation.surface: A rider wonders what ails a horse that has been out among the geese on the left of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Problem horse may have' looks like a description of a difficult animal, but it defines a disease horses can catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Glanders is a contagious bacterial infection of horses, an illness they may suffer.

clue.text: Lass on trail of flautist

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl or lass
a trail is a path or way

explanation.surface: A girl follows the path taken by a flute player.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a famous name: Sir James Galway, the Northern Irish flute virtuoso.
explanation.definitionFit: James Galway is a world-famous Irish flute player, so the surname stands for a flautist.

clue.text: Coquette not entirely up for entering a game or seasonal jape

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside the other, here into A plus the game

parts.note: pool is the cue game played on a table

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the trimmed word is read from bottom to top, backwards
not entirely means the word for coquette loses its last letter

parts.note: a coquette is a flirt

explanation.surface: A teasing woman gets involved in a game, or plays a trick at a certain time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims the coquette to FLIR and 'up' turns that to RILF; 'game' is the pool of the pool hall, not a match.
explanation.definitionFit: An April fool is a prank played on 1 April, a jape tied to one day of the year.

clue.text: Jazzman's version of "O! The Grand Jardin!"

definitions.note: the possessive is a link: the jazzman's version, so the definition is the jazzman himself

indicators.note: a version of the quoted words is a new arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A jazz musician performs his own rendering of a song titled after a grand garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation's fifteen letters are rearranged to give the guitarist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Django Reinhardt was the Belgian-born Romani guitarist who pioneered gypsy jazz.

clue.text: Twitch about during authentic performance

indicators.note: during means the turned word sits inside the word for authentic

parts.note: real means authentic

indicators.note: about means the word for twitch is turned round

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A performer's nervous twitch appears in the middle of a genuine show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives CIT; 'authentic performance' tempts as one phrase, but only 'performance' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical or poetry performance, often by a single artist.

clue.text: Work, sit or stand up to

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: A list of choices: get to work, sit tight, or put up resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose someone is to resist or confront them, which is to stand up to them.

clue.text: Rotten borough map Plath found in picture book

indicators.note: rotten means spoilt or broken down, so these letters fall apart and re-form

explanation.surface: A corrupt old constituency appears on a map belonging to the poet Sylvia Plath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten borough' looks like the historical term for a corrupt English seat with few voters, but 'Rotten' is the anagram signal for BOROUGH MAP PLATH.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph album is a book for holding pictures, literally a picture book.

clue.text: Undisguised, boy's lost right to be upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards
lost means the boy's name loses a letter

parts.note: Trevor is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad loses his right to something and is upset about it.
explanation.walkthrough: TREVOR loses its last R, giving TREVO; 'to be upset' turns that into the answer. The 's means 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, not hidden or disguised in any way.

clue.text: Topless god introducing bird to the life everlasting

indicators.note: introducing means the bird is brought into the trimmed word
in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a deity is a god
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A god without a top has a bird brought to him for eternal life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' leaves EITY; the bird lands just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is endless time, the life everlasting of religious belief.

clue.text: Mate mostly upset by snare

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned over, so the letters read in reverse
mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: Someone's partner is mostly annoyed at being caught in a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTNER without its last R is PARTNE; 'upset' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to catch in a trap, just as a snare does.

clue.text: Note about a rendition of scripture in early form

indicators.note: about means note and a go around the Bible version

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible, a rendering of scripture

explanation.surface: A musical note surrounds a version of the Bible in its first form.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the immature stage of an insect, the creature's early form before change.

clue.text: Rod grasping inflections of language

indicators.note: grasping means the rod holds the inflections inside it

parts.note: a cane is a rod
tones are the inflections of the voice

explanation.surface: A stick seems to take hold of the varying tones of a spoken language.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the language really does use tones to tell words apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantonese is the Chinese language of Guangdong and Hong Kong.

clue.text: Animal, totally Russian, devouring a Turk's head

parts.note: all means totally

indicators.note: devouring means the Russian swallows the other letters inside him

parts.note: Igor is a typical Russian man's name

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word Turk

explanation.surface: A creature that, like a Russian, eats a Turk's head entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: An alligator is a large reptile, a kind of animal.

clue.text: Frequently decimal

definitions.meaning: read as two words, decimal means based on, or consisting ...

explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently; split as 'of ten' it describes something decimal, counted in tens.

clue.text: Herb supplied by Klingsor, reluctantly

indicators.note: supplied by means the letters are provided from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A herb is grudgingly handed over by Klingsor, the magician in Wagner's opera Parsifal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrel is a sharp-tasting leafy plant used in cooking, a culinary herb.

clue.text: Defence of impersonator getting into character

indicators.note: getting into means the impersonator goes inside the character

parts.note: a part is a character an actor plays
an ape is a mimic, one who apes or impersonates

explanation.surface: A mimic gets into a role so deeply he needs protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall on a rampart or bridge, a defence.

clue.text: Territory (French, yes?) inhaling Luxembourg's scent

parts.note: a patch is a territory, as of a salesman or gang

indicators.note: inhaling means the French word breathes in the letter for Luxembourg

parts.note: oui is French for yes
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a French region breathes in a fragrance from Luxembourg.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchouli is a heavy perfume from the oil of an Asian plant, a scent.

clue.text: Oilmen absorbing papers, mostly, with coffee

indicators.note: absorbing means the oil company takes in the trimmed word

parts.note: Esso is an oil company, so its staff are oilmen

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the press means the newspapers

explanation.surface: Oil workers read most of the papers over their coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' leaves PRES; Esso is the Exxon brand familiar in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An espresso is a strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Flies off in silence, being inconsiderate

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters are placed within the call for silence

parts.note: sh is a call for silence

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so the letters of flies are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone takes off in silence, rudely leaving without a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' makes ELFI; 'Flies off' reads as a hasty exit, but the flies are just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfish means thinking only of oneself, and so being thoughtless of others.

clue.text: Cry of anger not beginning to stifle student

indicators.note: to stifle means the letter for student is smothered inside the trimmed word
not beginning means the first letter is removed

parts.note: choler is an old word for anger
L is for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: An angry shout is not allowed to start because it is suppressed by a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cry of anger' looks like the definition, but only 'Cry' is. CHOLER without its C gives HOLER, with L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To holler is to shout or yell, a loud cry.

clue.text: Sidekick's obligation to hold games back

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', a link; the definition is the sidekick

indicators.note: to hold means the duty keeps the turned letters inside it

parts.note: duty is an obligation

indicators.note: back means the letters for games are reversed

parts.note: PE is physical education, school games

explanation.surface: An assistant feels obliged to hold back the games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives EP; 'games' at school in Britain are PE lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy is a second in command, an assistant or sidekick to a sheriff or leader.

clue.text: Screen submariner suppressing primordial urges

indicators.note: suppressing means the submariner holds the urges down inside himself

parts.note: a diver works under the sea
the id is the Freudian name for the primitive instinctual drives

explanation.surface: A submarine crewman tries to hide his basic instincts.
explanation.definitionFit: A divider is a screen or partition that separates a room.

clue.text: Kidnap smackhead, of course

parts.note: read as the head of smack, the first letter S
natch is slang for naturally, of course

explanation.surface: A heroin addict, naturally, carries out an abduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smackhead' is slang for a heroin user, but here it is the head of 'smack', its first letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: To snatch someone is to seize or abduct them, to kidnap.

clue.text: Appear unwell as low-lifer's decapitated

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: a wretch is a despicable person, a low-lifer; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone looks ill on seeing that a lowlife has been beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to heave as if vomiting, a clear sign of being unwell.

clue.text: Writer's double

definitions.meaning: the American author of Huckleberry Finn wrote under this pen name; the 's means 'is'
an old word meaning two, a pair

explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain is the pen name of Samuel Clemens; as an archaic word it means two or a pair.

clue.text: Heat anvil; forge monster

indicators.note: to forge is to shape metal anew, so these letters are hammered into a new order

explanation.surface: Blacksmithing instructions: heat the anvil and forge a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forge' looks like a noun naming the smithy, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Leviathan is the biblical sea monster, now any huge creature.

clue.text: Way to meet bimbo on landing

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
an airhead is a silly empty-headed person

explanation.surface: A suggestion for how to meet a silly young woman as one arrives on the stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stairhead is the landing at the top of a flight of stairs.

clue.text: Principal strength of second-rate weakling

parts.note: B is a second-class grade
a runt is the weakest of a litter

explanation.surface: A remark on the main power of a feeble and inferior creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The brunt is the main force or impact of something, as in bearing the brunt.

clue.text: Talk about name being highly decorated!

indicators.note: about means the word for talk goes around the letter for name

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Speaking at length about a name that has won many medals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately ornamented, very highly decorated.

clue.text: Dowdy drinker bites bum

indicators.note: bites means the drinker holds the other word inside it, as in its mouth

parts.note: to drink like a fish, so a fish is a heavy drinker
the rump is the buttocks, the bum

explanation.surface: A drunk sinks his teeth into someone's backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Frumpish means drab and unfashionable in dress, which is to say dowdy.
